title: Zoom
subtitle: Forward video instead of meshing or mixing it, and show each person only the tiles they can use
motto: Send each stream once, and let the server decide who needs it
keyInsight: An SFU turns each person's upload into one stream, but forwarding N-1 streams to N people makes server bandwidth grow with the square of meeting size, so the real fix is to send fewer streams.

decisions.title: Forward with an SFU instead of meshing or mixing
decisions.description: Each person uploads one stream and the server forwards copies, so client upload stays at 5 Mbit/s and latency stays near 100 ms.
decisions.alternatives: A peer-to-peer mesh needs 45 Mbit/s of upload in a 10-person call, and an MCU mixes on the server at about 200 ms and a heavy CPU cost.

decisions.title: Show a limited gallery
decisions.description: Sending each client at most 9 tiles keeps download at 13.5 Mbit/s and holds the fleet at 67,581 servers even for a 100-person meeting.
decisions.alternatives: Forwarding every stream to every person costs 8.3x the fleet at 100 people and does not fit a home connection.
